source: SPM 2026 Trial · WPKL · English Paper 2 · Part 3 Q5 · Story, 200–250 words
paragraphs: The silence of the night was broken by the sound of shattering glass. I sat up in bed, my heart pounding against my chest. The clock read 2 a.m., and the noise had come from Mak Cik Siti's house next door.

Peeking through my window, I saw a masked man climbing through her broken kitchen window. Mak Cik Siti, a frail seventy-year-old widow, lived alone, so I rushed to wake my father, a retired soldier who always kept a cool head in a crisis. I knew she was in grave danger.

Without wasting a second, my father called the police while I alerted our neighbours through the residents' WhatsApp group. Within minutes, several men armed with torches had quietly surrounded the house, blocking every escape route. When the burglar tried to flee through the back door, he found himself cornered.

Soon, the wail of sirens filled the air, and the police arrived to arrest the burglar. They found Mak Cik Siti's jewellery and savings stuffed in his bag. Thankfully, she was shaken but unharmed. After that night, the residents set up a neighbourhood patrol to keep the area safe. Everyone took turns to watch over the street.
The next morning, Mak Cik Siti came over with a plate of kuih and tears of gratitude in her eyes. That night taught me that a united community is the best protection of all.
